newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed warns of Chechen trouble after his sacking.
newsitem.headline: Lebed warns of Chechen trouble after his sacking.

text.p: Alexander Lebed warned on Thursday that events in breakaway Chechnya would get worse after President Boris Yeltsin sacked him as Russia's security chief. Lebed has signed a peace deal with Chechen rebels.
Lebed told Ekho Moskvy radio he would stay in politics but would "proceed in a completely legal way".
Lebed, in what appeared to be his first comment since Yeltsin sacked him in a dramatic televised appearance, said: "I am not worried...I've never begged and will never beg."
Asked whether he expected events in Chechnya to go according to "the worst possible scenario" after his dismissal, Lebed answered: "In all probability, yes".
"It is my business who I choose as friends," Lebed said commenting on Yeltsin's accusations over his alliance with the president's former bodyguard and confidant Alexander Korzhakov.
"I can no longer tolerate this situation and I am forced to relieve General Lebed of his position as secretary of the Security Council," Yeltsin said, signing a decree as he spoke.
"I have told Lebed to learn to work with other state bodies and leaders...he did not learn his lesson. Lately he allowed himself a number of mistakes which are impermissable in Russia's interests."

Yeltsin, who spoke forcefully but looked rigid in an appearance which only showed the top half of his body, brought Lebed into his team after the reserve general scored a strong 15 percent in the first round of Russia's presidential election.
But Lebed has won few friends in the Kremlin and Interior Ministry Anatoly Kulikov on Wednesday accused him of plotting a "creeping coup" and trying to seize power. Lebed denied the charges.
